- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast for next 5–7 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 75), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 1–3% below peak for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (price drops 5–10% from recent peak), model often fails to recognize it; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average.  
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates early in the forecast window (first 5–7 days); apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per day for first 7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead of sentiment peak or trough.
